sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the missing word in a line they haven't seen ("time and ___ happen to all"). Nothing on the earlier cards lets them reason to "chance" over "trouble" or "judgment", so this is a guess at wording.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The blank tests the exact wording of the line ("eat your bread with ___"). Joy, care and haste are all plausible, and the baker can only pick the right one by guessing the verse's phrase.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The True statement repeats "eat your bread with joy", which card 2 just asked and answered. It re-asks the same fact, with only "God has already approved your works" added.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question. An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.
